title: P0 hosted API multiplex controller hedging failchain analysis
summary: Short summary: On 2028-04-22 we observed a cascading outage impacting hosted-api streaming sessions. A recent hedging change in the multiplex controller caused parallel hedges to escalate under certain request patterns, amplifying acceptor/backlog pressure and triggering KV-cache lock contention in a subset of shards. Symptoms were increased streaming silence (partial streams with no finalization), elevated p95/p99 tail latency, and a rise in 5xx from edge to runtime. Estimated customer impact: intermittent failures for ~2% of global streaming sessions during a 36-minute window. This document records timeline, root cause hypothesis, immediate mitigations, and long-term action items.
incident_timeline:
2028-04-22 14:02 UTC - Alert: streaming silence anomaly (p50/95/99 divergence) triggered from streaming-health dashboard
2028-04-22 14:04 UTC - Ops oncall (Aisha) triaged: increase in 5xx from edge -> runtime and concurrent acceptor backlog spikes noted in telemetry
2028-04-22 14:07 UTC - Pager escalated to SRE pager rotation; initial hypothesis: autoscaler or tokenization regression
2028-04-22 14:12 UTC - Heap of active accepts on multiplex controller seen; spike correlated with hedging metric increase (hedge_fanout_count)
2028-04-22 14:15 UTC - Feature flip: disable new hedging config for multiplex controller (config rollback) initiated by Diego; telemetry begin to show partial improvement
2028-04-22 14:22 UTC - Full rollback confirmed; acceptor backlog subsiding but KV cache lock contention persisted on 3 shards
2028-04-22 14:34 UTC - Emergency parameter change: increased acceptor queue depth and temporary increase to prefetch workers on affected shards (Marcus) to drain backlog
2028-04-22 14:38 UTC - Streaming success rates returning to baseline; alerts cleared at 14:48 after sustained recovery
2028-04-22 15:00 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; post-incident investigation kicked off
impact:
Observed metrics during incident window (14:02-14:48 UTC):
- Streaming session failures (partial/no-final): peak 37% of sessions for specific shard group (global weighted ~2% of streaming traffic)
- 5xx rate (edge->runtime): 15x baseline during peak 14:10-14:18
- p95 latency for non-streaming generation endpoints jumped from 220ms to ~1.2s for affected ops
- No customer data loss observed; incomplete streams were retriable by clients
- A small set of customers reported degraded UX and increased client-side reconnects (CS notified via CS-EMERG ticket)
root_cause:
Primary cause: a hedging algorithm change merged three days earlier (PR 5142) adjusted the hedging policy to be more aggressive for multiplexed streaming requests. Under a realistic high-variance prefix mix (many short prefix pops + periodic long tokens), the controller triggered parallel hedges for the same logical session across replicas. The hedging code lacked a soft-debounce/circuit-breaker for concurrent hedges per-session and did not decrement the hedging counter reliably on certain early-exit paths (race). This produced transient amplification: multiple hedges created overlapping inflight request groups, increasing acceptor queue pressure and producing head-of-line effects.
Secondary contributors: 
- KV cache lock contention: amplified by multiple simultaneous cache warms on the same key range; our cache locking is coarse-grained per-shard and became a bottleneck when hedging simultaneously triggered cache rehydration on several workers.
- Observability blind spot: no direct metric for per-session-hedge-concurrency; hedging fanout was only monitored as aggregated count which hid pathological per-session spikes.
- Runbook gap: hedging rollbacks and the interplay with acceptor queue tuning were not documented in any runbook; initial responders spent critical minutes validating hypotheses and locating the relevant config flag.
immediate_mitigation:
Actions taken during incident: 
- Rollback hedging config: reverted PR 5142 feature flag at 14:15 (Diego)
- Increased acceptor queue depth and prefetch workers on affected shards to accelerate drain (Marcus)
- Temporarily disabled aggressive cache rehydration path for multiplex controller to reduce lock contention (Fiona)
- CS notified top affected customers and routed them to support channel; support provided guidance to retry streams with exponential backoff
- Post-rollback monitoring: enable high-frequency sampling of hedge_fanout_count and acceptor_queue_length for 2 hours after incident
Effectiveness: rollback eliminated hedge fanout spikes within ~7 minutes; backlog drain and cache contention subsided within ~20 minutes. The combined mitigations prevented further customer-visible impact.
long_term_followups:
Planned followups and engineering work: 
1) Hedging safety: implement per-session hedging circuit breaker and ensure hedging counter decrement on all exit paths (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2028-05-06)
2) Hedging canary pipeline: add targeted canary for multiplexer hedging that simulates skewed prefix distributions and checks for acceptor/backlog amplification before rollout (owner: Samir Patel, due: 2028-05-13)
3) Fine-grained metrics: add per-session/max-concurrent-hedges metric and expose percentile distribution; add alert when per-session hedges > 1 for >30s (owner: Diego Martinez, due: 2028-05-01)
4) KV cache locking: investigate finer-grained cache locks or async rehydration to avoid blocking on hot keys; prototype due 2028-06-01 (owner: Marcus Li)
5) Runbook update: add explicit hedging rollback steps, and note interaction with acceptor queue tuning and cache flags (owner: Aisha Kumar, due: 2028-04-30)
6) Post-deploy test harness: augment preflight with spike-sim tests for streaming patterns that historically caused issues (owner: Fiona Chen, due: 2028-05-20)
7) SLA/comms: review CS playbook for streaming degradation notifications to reduce manual triage time (owner: Customer Success lead, due: 2028-05-10)
monitor_playbook:
Immediate alerts to add or tune: 
- Add alert: per-session hedging_concurrency > 1 (p95) for >30s -> P1
- Add alert: acceptor_queue_length per-shard > 75% capacity for 2m -> P1
- Add alert: kv_cache_lock_wait_ms (p99) > 200ms -> P2
- Dashboard: hedging_fanout_count (by shard, by session bucket) and a dedicated streaming-hedging-scrub view (ops mode)
- Runbook steps (short): 
  1) Identify if hedging fanout spike is present: query hedge_fanout_count by session_id sample
  2) If hedging fanout spike confirmed, flip hedging feature flag off (or throttle via dynamic config)
  3) If acceptor backlog > threshold, increase queue depth and add workers on affected shards to drain backlog; follow capacity playbook to ensure memory headroom
  4) If kv lock wait high, temporarily disable synchronous cache rehydration path and enable async fallback
  5) Notify CS & SRE leads; escalate to engineering owning hedging code if rollback doesn't reduce traffic within 10m

notes:
Additional context and hypotheses: 
- The hedging change was intended to reduce tail latency on certain long-running sessions; however the absence of per-session rate limiting allowed it to cascade under mixed workloads.
- We should consider toggling hedging to operate with a token bucket or similar limiter per-session to prevent amplification.
- Client-side behavior: many clients aggressively reconnect on partial streams which can increase backend load; CS/SDK team should evaluate backoff defaults.
- Post-incident retrospective scheduled 2028-04-27 15:00 UTC with eng-sre, serving-runtime owners, and product-hosted-api stakeholders.
